_doc: Host inventory for the ops scripts and skills: the production server and the
compute nodes that run the standalone forecast cycle off-box. Copy this file
to deploy/hosts.json (gitignored) and fill in the real hosts. Resolve paths
with scripts/ops/hosts.py -- it reads this file, then checks each path on the
host itself, so a stale entry shows up as a problem instead of a wrong path.
Why a file and not the agent's memory: a deploy step that silently skips a
node because nobody remembered it fails quietly. A missing file is loud; a
faulty recollection is not. Host details are deployment-private, so the real
inventory stays untracked while this example keeps the contract reviewable.
Cloud sessions have no hosts.json by design (no host access from there).
server fields:
name              short label used in output
ssh               ssh target, exactly as you would type it
hostname          optional: short hostname the ssh target must reach;
catches a DNS/ssh alias that points at the wrong machine
project_dir       checkout on the server, relative to the ssh user's home
container         docker container that must be running and healthy
url               public base URL (health checks, deploy notifications)
node fields:
name              short label used in deploy output
ssh               ssh target, exactly as you would type it
hostname          optional but recommended: as for the server
repo              checkout path on the node (may use ~)
branch            branch the node should track; deploys use --ff-only
venv              venv path relative to repo, for dependency reinstalls
region            artifact region prefix this node emits (eu | us)
runner            the cycle script the scheduler invokes
schedule_utc      when the node starts, UTC, for the racing-a-cycle check
cycle_minutes     rough cycle duration, to judge whether one is in flight
healthcheck_slug  healthchecks.io slug the runner pings on success
os                macos | linux -- decides launchd vs cron for schedules
lan_only          true when the host is only reachable from its own network
(mDNS .local names, private IPs). hosts.py and the deploy
skill report an unreachable lan_only node as 'could not
tell', not as down -- expected when away from that network.
notes             anything a human needs before touching the box

nodes.name: example-node
nodes.notes: Replace with the real node. Keep schedule_utc accurate -- the deploy skill uses it to avoid pulling mid-cycle.
